alternative: Pass the scoped value explicitly: context.Context as the first parameter of every function on the request path (context.WithValue plus a typed accessor, or a dedicated struct), or keep the state in the struct that owns the goroutine. sync.Pool is only for reusable buffers without identity - its entries may be dropped at any GC - so it is not a place to store request state.
idiom_name: none - goroutine-local storage does not exist by design; context.Context is passed explicitly
implementation_notes: Go has no goroutine-local storage and deliberately exposes no goroutine id: the FAQ explains that goroutines are anonymous workers and that naming one makes it special, and the Go team's position is that there should be no way to obtain a goroutine id and no goroutine local storage (golang/go#22770). The runtime also offers no thread-keyed store, because many goroutines share one OS thread and goroutines may migrate, so a thread-keyed value would silently belong to the wrong unit of work. The replacement is explicit propagation: context.Context as the first parameter of every function on the request path, carrying only request-scoped values, with keys as unexported types and typed accessors (pkg.go.dev/context, go.dev/blog/context), or state owned by the struct that represents the goroutine's work. Hand-rolled goroutine-local maps keyed by a parsed goroutine id exist outside the standard library but read the runtime stack, take a lock per access, and break as soon as any handler or library spawns another goroutine.
pitfalls: A goroutine started by a library does not inherit anything: the context must be passed to it explicitly, which is why context-checking linters exist for dropped ctx values.
sync.Pool is not a substitute for per-goroutine state: entries are shared and may be removed at any GC, so it is safe only for scratch buffers that carry no identity.
Storing mutable request state in context values is itself discouraged - context values are for data that transits API boundaries, not for optional parameters or mutable business state.
